lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Tomas Kessler — you don't know the name yet — lies with his cheek to the stone, one arm folded under him as if he fell asleep mid-sentence. The rain has been washing him for hours.

responses.text: [Perception] Press his chest. Listen to what comes up.
[Step back. Let the dead keep their counsel.]

lines.speaker: attribute
lines.text: The runoff pools toward him, not from him. He didn't crawl out of the harbour and collapse. The harbour was brought to him — or he was brought to the harbour and set back down. Either way: he was moved.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You roll back the ruined wool, part the wet shirt. The skin is grey and perfect. No blade, no bruise, no rope-burn, no needle.

lines.speaker: attribute
lines.text: No wound. Catalogue it and move on — a man does not simply stop. Something filled him or emptied him. Find which.

lines.speaker: attribute
lines.text: Your eyes slide off him. The cold has your hands shaking and your thoughts are a deck of cards dropped down a stairwell. Steady — try again when you've collected yourself.

lines.speaker: attribute
lines.text: Or don't. The dead are patient. The living, watching you fumble a corpse, are not.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You press below the sternum. A thin run of water rises at the corner of his mouth, and you taste the air above it: salt. Harbour-salt.

lines.speaker: attribute
lines.text: Seawater in the lungs. He drowned. And yet —

lines.speaker: attribute
lines.text: — and yet he's lying on dry stone, above the tideline, with his shoe set neatly beside him. A drowned man does not tuck himself in. Two facts that refuse to share a room.

responses.text: [The water and the dry stone don't agree. File the contradiction.]
[Enough. The rest is for the living to answer.]

lines.speaker: attribute
lines.text: Hold those two facts up to the light together and a third stands behind them, waiting. Open the case board when you're ready to make them speak.

lines.speaker: attribute
lines.text: Nothing. The rain has been at him too long, washing the story off his skin. Come back when your eyes are sharper — or your hands steadier.
